children.text: Storytelling has evolved from stories shared around campfires, to written works, to theatre performances, to movies, television shows, and to video games. The ways stories are communicated are constantly changing and evolving.

The earliest genre was the genre of the Romantic Quest, which inspired the arc of the romance novel as we understand it now. The quest structure eventually evolved into fantasy as well, with the ideas of mystical worlds and magic systems unfurling from fairytales. History makes its reappearances in historical fiction, where authors consider how the current context of our world fits into the future. Science fiction became a warning of the threat of technological advancement, and what would happen if things went too far. There are dozens of genres, with subgenres emerging from the existing story structures, or hybridisations. Romantasy is one of the most popular, with the romance structure becoming blended with fantasy worlds and magic systems.

These genres allow audiences to better understand the world, in the ways it does, and could have existed. Storytelling will always be an art form, and one that is ever-changing, and is always an act of creative experimentation.

title: The Genres and Forms of Storytelling
